title: Fan charts, their pulled log ideals, and lifted fan towers
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian fine saturated log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and let $F$ be a fine fan [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. A fan chart consists of a Zariski log structure on $X$ and a morphism from its sharp monoidal space to $F$ inducing bijections on all monoid stalks. The sharp space is the sheafification of the unit quotient of the Zariski restriction of the actual log sheaf. For a fan ideal $J$, its pulled log ideal is the inverse image in the log sheaf of the ideal generated by the image of $J$ in the characteristic sheaf; membership is tested at all geometric germs, including multiplication by log sections and unit multiples. Given a finite saturated fan blowup tower $T$ with its ordered centers, a lifted log fan tower consists of an fs log scheme $X_i$ and a fan chart $c_i:X_i\to T_i$ at every level, and log maps $X_{i+1}\to X_i$ which are saturated log blowups along $c_i^*J_i$. Every log/fan square commutes on the actual characteristic germs under the canonical section-induced relation [def-per-strict-log-morphism]. This packages a given lift with all its centers and charts; it does not assert that a lift exists. Length zero, empty log schemes and empty fans are allowed.
